To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the minimal buffering requirement is proportional (not constant) to the parameters of AIMD algorithm and the application's sending rates and round-trip-times, (2) the minimal buffering cost is proportional to the square of the application's sending bit rate, (3) the minimal buffering costs are higher for applications that have longer round-trip-times (i.e., applications that have longer delay to the network congestion point).

the amount of buffering needed to adapt to congestion control oscillations is proportional to the rate and the round-trip-time and that this buffering requirement increases as the application rate increases.

the minimal buffering requirements for congestion-controlled interactive multimedia applications are proportional to the parameters in the AIMD algorithm, and are quadratic to the application bit-rate and round-trip time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of congestion control mechanisms that can be used by interactive multimedia applications.
the minimal buffering requirements and the delay costs of congestion-controlled interactive multimedia applications.
the minimal buffering requirements for interactive multimedia applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for interactive multimedia applications, the minimal buffering requirement is proportional the product of application's sending rate, round-trip-time, and AIMD parameters.
the minimal buffer requirements for congestion controlled interactive multimedia applications depend on the adaptation policy used and the parameters of the congestion control algorithm.

the minimal buffering requirement of congestion controlled multimedia is proportional to the round-trip-time, proportional to the sending rate and proportional to the congestion control algorithm parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the minimal buffering requirement is an important design parameter for interactive multimedia applications.

, for interactive multimedia applications with a fixed sending rate and a fixed round-trip-time, the minimal buffering requirement is proportional the sending rate and roundtrip-time and inversely proportional to the congestion control parameters.
the minimal buffering requirement is a function of the application's sending rates, round-trip-times and parameters of the AIM D algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
applications should not blindly follow the maximization-of-throughput adaptation policies.
applications should not adapt their sending rates exactly to available bandwidth.
there exists a tradeoff between maximizing throughput and reducing delay cost.
